solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Famous actor keeping to part that's not moving

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: a famous actor is a star
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrated actor sticks to a role in which he never has to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' suggests a stage role, but here it is a machine part.
explanation.definitionFit: A stator is the stationary component of a motor or generator, as opposed to the rotating rotor.

clue.text: Keep tenor in reserve for last piece

indicators.note: to keep something in a place is to hold it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a sub is a substitute player held in reserve
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: A choir director keeps a tenor on the bench for the final piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside SUB to give STUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A stub is the short remaining end of something, such as a pencil or cigarette, the bit that is left over.

clue.text: Body parts cut in short supply

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, it means flexibly, so the letters are bent into a new order
one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: the letters of short rearranged
to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: Body parts are being cut because they are in short supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short supply' looks like a fixed phrase, but 'supply' is the adverb from supple, signalling a rearrangement of 'short'; AXE goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoraxes are chests, the parts of the body between neck and abdomen, in their regular plural.

clue.text: Act includes comedy accepted in foreign language

indicators.note: something that includes other things holds them inside it

blocks.note: a turn is a performer's act on a variety bill
short for comedy, as in romcom
A is the abbreviation for accepted

explanation.surface: A stage act with comic material goes down well when performed in a foreign tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: A turn is the variety-hall word for a performer's act.
explanation.definitionFit: Turcoman, or Turkmen, is the Turkic language spoken in Turkmenistan and neighbouring regions.

clue.text: Chopped Indian dish indeed served up inside for peasant

indicators.note: something chopped has had its end cut off, so the last letter goes
in a down clue, served up means brought upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top
one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: raita is a yoghurt side dish from India
ay is an old form of yes, indeed

explanation.surface: A peasant is served a chopped-up Indian dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Raita is a yoghurt-and-cucumber side dish; 'served up' sounds culinary but turns the short word upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A raiyat or ryot is an Indian tenant farmer or smallholder, the term for a peasant cultivator.

clue.text: Is lamb, say first for hotpot or duck?

indicators.note: first for asks for the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: is shortened to 's, as in it's
lamb is an example of meat
the opening letter of hotpot

explanation.surface: A cook wonders whether lamb or duck should go first into a hotpot; a Lancashire hotpot is a lamb stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Smeath is a dialect name for the smew, a small diving duck.

clue.text: Idler coming from very absorbing chat

indicators.note: something absorbing soaks up and holds another thing inside it

blocks.note: so means very, as in so good
a chat is a talk

explanation.surface: A layabout emerges from a really gripping conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absorbing' looks like an adjective for the chat, but it is the wrapping signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalko is an Anglo-Irish term for a penniless gentleman who has no occupation, a loafer.

clue.text: Stadium publicity put out about gap in fence

indicators.note: something put out is ejected, so those letters leave the word
turned about, the remaining letters are moved around into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
an ad is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: Advertising hoardings at a stadium are thrown out over a hole in the perimeter fence.
explanation.walkthrough: STADIUM without AD leaves STIUM, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A musit is an old word for a hole or gap in a hedge or fence through which a hare passes.

clue.text: Assembling a mass of separate things not good for exam

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is taken out

blocks.clueFragment: Assembling a mass of separate things
blocks.note: aggregation is the collecting of separate units into a mass
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Gathering lots of separate facts together is not a good way to prepare for an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: One G is dropped from AGGREGATION.
explanation.definitionFit: The agrégation is the French competitive examination for teaching posts in lycées and universities.

clue.text: Endless mess on pass is troubling

indicators.note: with no end, the final letter is cut off
in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so the first piece comes before the second

blocks.note: to make a hash of something is to make a mess of it
to sling is to throw or pass something casually

explanation.surface: A footballer's endless mess-ups with the pass are a worry.
explanation.walkthrough: To sling is to toss something across, a casual way to pass it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hassling means bothering or harassing someone, the same as giving them trouble.

clue.text: Deprived of love, abandoned to huge trauma? David Copperfield perhaps

indicators.note: deprived of means lacking, so that letter is removed
abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose into a new order

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unloved boy abandoned to great suffering sounds like Dickens's David Copperfield.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dickens orphan is the false path; the David Copperfield meant is the American stage illusionist.
explanation.definitionFit: A thaumaturge is a wonder-worker or magician, and David Copperfield is a famous illusionist, so he is an example.

clue.text: Massage one attempts Sweden exported?

indicators.note: something exported is sent out of the country, so that letter leaves
to massage is to knead and work over, so the letters are kneaded into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Someone tries a Swedish massage, wondering if it was an export from Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: Swedish massage is a technique sent abroad from Sweden, and this is one of its strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapotement is the rhythmic tapping or percussion stroke used in Swedish massage.

clue.text: Investment authority once last to encompass very small change overseas

indicators.note: last to asks for the final letter belonging to the following word

blocks.note: the Personal Investment Authority, a former UK regulator
the final letter of encompass
très is French for very

explanation.surface: A former regulator would encompass even very small sums of foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Encompass' looks like a containment signal, but only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Piastres are coins of low value in several Middle Eastern countries, such as Egypt and Lebanon.

clue.text: Shoot nameless dog for the chase

indicators.note: without a name, so the abbreviation for name is dropped

blocks.note: a branch is a shoot of a tree

explanation.surface: A hunter shoots an unnamed dog that was chasing game.
explanation.walkthrough: N for name is taken out of BRANCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A brach is an old word for a hound, especially a scent hound bitch used in hunting.

clue.text: Fanciful birds not extinct seen on arms regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, at even intervals

blocks.note: something not extinct is still live
the second and fourth letters of arms

explanation.surface: Imaginary birds that survive only on coats of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liver Birds are the mythical cormorant-like birds on Liverpool's coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A liver is a heraldic bird, an imaginary creature shown on the arms of Liverpool.

clue.text: Fruit, one best when on the turn

indicators.note: turning round means the whole sequence is read backwards

blocks.note: a means one
top means best
as means when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit is at its best just as it begins to go off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the turn' looks like fruit going off, but it reverses A, TOP, AS.
explanation.definitionFit: The sapota, or sapodilla, is a tropical American tree bearing a sweet brown fruit.

clue.text: Dogs barking some days

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters go crazy into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dogs bark on certain days.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is British slang for mad, the signal here, though it fits dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Samoyeds are a breed of white Siberian spitz dog, originally used for herding and sledging.

clue.text: Getting rid of waste a big problem for Brussels once

blocks.note: the European Community, the former name for the EU based in Brussels
a crisis is a serious problem

explanation.surface: Waste disposal was once a headache for the Brussels bureaucrats.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are taken in reverse of clue order: EC then CRISIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccrisis is a medical term for excretion, the expulsion of waste matter from the body.

clue.text: Brass once used by Beethoven and Brahms making their mark

definitions.text: Brass once used by Beethoven and Brahms making their mark

blocks.clueFragment: Brass once used by Beethoven and Brahms
blocks.note: surface reading: the brass section of the orchestra in the great German composers' symphonies
setter's reading: brass is slang for money, and a hundred of these old German coins made one Mark

explanation.surface: Brass instruments played a big part in how Beethoven and Brahms made their name.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass means money in British slang; the German Mark was divided into a hundred smaller coins, now replaced by the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The coins were the hundredth parts of the German Mark, the currency in use in Germany before the euro.

clue.text: Disguised mafioso foremost in chartering tourist boats in Italy

indicators.note: foremost picks the leading letter of each of the next words
a disguised thing has its appearance changed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letters of chartering and tourist

explanation.surface: A gangster in disguise hires out tourist boats in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Motoscafi are Italian motorboats, such as the water taxis of Venice; the word is the plural of motoscafo.

clue.text: Found US short on segments of animal

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: found, as in came across, is met
the US is America

explanation.surface: Someone found the US lacking in parts of animals, perhaps in a zoology report.
explanation.definitionFit: Metameric describes an animal body divided into repeated segments, as in earthworms; it relates to those segments.

clue.text: Left energised after Cuba recalled

indicators.note: something recalled is withdrawn, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: excited means energised, stirred up
C is the international vehicle code for Cuba

explanation.surface: Someone departed, full of energy, after being called back from Cuba.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' tempts as a reversal; here it means withdrawn, so C leaves EXCITED.
explanation.definitionFit: Exited means went out or departed, the same as left a place.

clue.text: Nick often short of time for fish

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: to nick is to steal, or rob
often means a lot
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Nick frequently runs out of time when he goes fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: The robalo is a tropical American sea fish, also called snook, valued as food and game.

clue.text: The Japanese film a French city with no end of remains

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
with no means lacking, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
Nîmes is a city in southern France
the final letter of remains

explanation.surface: A Japanese film is set in a French city where only ruins remain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of remains' looks like 'plenty of ruins'; it means NIMES without the last letter of remains, its own final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Anime is the Japanese style of animated film and television, so the term names that kind of cinema.

clue.text: Rowing about cutting oil seal

indicators.note: something cutting into another goes inside it

blocks.note: an O-ring is a rubber ring used as an oil seal
A is an abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: A rowing boat's engine has a cut around its oil seal.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside O-RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaring is the act of working an oar, that is, propelling a boat by rowing.

clue.text: The old soldiers leading one Middle Easterner

indicators.note: pieces that lead go in front of what follows them

blocks.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
soldiers are men in the ranks
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Veteran soldiers lead the way for a man from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: Ye is the old spelling of 'the' seen in shop names like Ye Olde Tea Shoppe.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yemeni is a native or citizen of Yemen, on the southern tip of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Consulting about current American offshoots

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: to con is to study or pore over, as when consulting a text
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Consultants gather round the latest American spin-off ventures.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside CONS. 'American' marks the US spelling of scions.
explanation.definitionFit: Cions is the American spelling of scions, young shoots or twigs cut for grafting.

clue.text: Heavy fall, tons shifted from side of hill facing glacier

indicators.note: something shifted from a place is moved away, so it is taken out

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for tons
stoss is the side of a hill that faces the oncoming glacier

explanation.surface: A landslide moves tons of rock down the hillside facing a glacier.
explanation.walkthrough: T comes out of STOSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Soss is a dialect word for a heavy, clumsy fall or a plump down onto something.

clue.text: Reclusive Italian seen behind lake in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse
behind places one piece after the other in the answer

blocks.note: a mere is a lake
Ital is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: A shy Italian is spotted hiding behind a lake on a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' suggests a hermit's hideaway, which fits the definition, but it only turns the lake round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eremital means relating to a hermit, so it describes someone who lives in solitude.

clue.text: Club selling mean and glossy works of art

indicators.note: to club is to beat, so the letters are battered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An art club sells polished pieces at a stingy price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a society selling work; it is a verb meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamellings are pieces decorated with fused glassy coatings, giving a shiny ornamental finish.

clue.text: Time bit of durra cropped

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a single letter taken from it, here the first

blocks.note: sithe is an archaic word for time
the opening letter of durra

explanation.surface: It is time for part of the durra crop to be harvested; durra is a grain sorghum.
explanation.definitionFit: Sithed is an old spelling of scythed, meaning mown or cut down with a scythe.

clue.text: Levy on outside broadcast making you think a lot

definitions.note: verb phrase: the answer means to make someone think a lot

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it, so the first-named piece goes second

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for outside broadcast
sess is a variant spelling of cess, a tax or levy

explanation.surface: A tax on outside broadcasts gives a broadcaster plenty to ponder.
explanation.walkthrough: Cess is an old word for a local tax, and sess is its variant spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To obsess is to preoccupy someone's mind continually, filling their thoughts.
